title: Levelwise K-injective towers compute additive functors applied levelwise
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive functor [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Write $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ and similarly for $\mathcal B$, with levelwise exactness, and let $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ apply $G$ levelwise. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $RG^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ be the total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] obtained by resolving a strict tower complex by a K-injective tower complex and applying $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ termwise. Here a tower complex $Q$ is K-injective when every chain map from an acyclic tower complex to $Q$ is null-homotopic; for ordinary module complexes use [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. If $X$ is a strict tower complex whose every evaluation $X_n$ is K-injective, then for every K-injective tower resolution $q:X\to Q$, every evaluation $Q_n$ is K-injective and
$$G^{\operatorname{Tow}}(q):G^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\longrightarrow G^{\operatorname{Tow}}Q$$
is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. Consequently the canonical comparison $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\to RG^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B))$, natural on the category of such $X$ and compatible with their strict transitions. In particular, if $X$ has the same K-injective complex $J$ at every level and a chain endomorphism $s:J\to J$ as each transition, its derived image is represented by the actual tower with terms $GJ$ and transitions $G(s)$.

proof.text: Fix a K-injective tower resolution $q:X\to Q$. Evaluation is exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so it computes cohomology levelwise: $H^r(q)_n=H^r(q_n)$. Thus each $q_n:X_n\to Q_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective] to the K-injective tower complex $Q$ to conclude that every $Q_n$ is K-injective. Its indexing by positive integers agrees with the cited opposite natural-number poset after the order isomorphism $n\mapsto n-1$. No injectivity of the individual terms of $Q$, or surjectivity of its transitions, is required.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof paragraph beginning "Note that the functor"; exact evaluation and the exact-left-adjoint argument

proof.text: Both $X_n$ (by hypothesis) and $Q_n$ (by step 1) are K-injective. The final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] applied to $q_n$ gives a chain homotopy inverse $v_n:Q_n\to X_n$, with $v_nq_n\simeq1_{X_n}$ and $q_nv_n\simeq1_{Q_n}$. These inverses are chosen separately at each level; no compatibility between the $v_n$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies

proof.text: By additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], $G(0)=0$ and $G(a-b)=G(a)-G(b)$. Applying $G$ to a chain homotopy equation $f-g=dh+hd$ gives $G(f)-G(g)=G(d)G(h)+G(h)G(d)$ degree by degree. Apply this to the two homotopies in step 2. Then $G(v_n)$ is a chain homotopy inverse of $G(q_n)$. Homotopic maps induce equal maps on $H^r=\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: on the kernel the difference $dh+hd$ lands in the image of $d$. Hence $H^r(G(q_n))$ has inverse $H^r(G(v_n))$, proving that $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}(q)$ is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies

proof.text: Put $T=G^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. The morphism $Tq:TX\to TQ$ is a strict tower map because $G$ preserves composition. Cohomology in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B)$ is computed levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Every component of $H^r(Tq)$ is invertible by step 3, and these inverses form a tower map: multiply the commuting transition square by the component inverses. Therefore $Tq$ is a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes. Its class $L_{\mathcal B}(Tq)$ is invertible in the derived category by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $L_{\mathcal A}$ and $L_{\mathcal B}$ denote the localization functors for the two tower categories.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies

proof.text: Use the total right derived functor $RT=RG^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ stipulated in the statement, with its unit $\eta$ as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Since $Q$ is K-injective as a tower, the cited computation property says that $\eta_Q$ is invertible. Also $RT(L_{\mathcal A}q)$ is invertible, since $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $c_q=\eta_Q^{-1}\circ RT(L_{\mathcal A}q):RT(L_{\mathcal A}X)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal B}(TQ)$. Naturality of the unit gives $c_q\circ\eta_X=L_{\mathcal B}(Tq)$. The right side is invertible by step 4, so $\eta_X$ is invertible. This identifies the asserted canonical comparison with the actual strict tower map $Tq$ under the resolution-computation isomorphism. The existence of the K-injective-resolution construction is part of the given $RT$, not an additional boundedness or exactness assumption on $G$.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies

proof.text: For a strict chain map $a:X\to Y$ between levelwise K-injective tower complexes, naturality of the same unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] reads $RT(L_{\mathcal A}a)\circ\eta_X=\eta_Y\circ L_{\mathcal B}(Ta)$. Thus the isomorphisms of step 5 give a natural comparison on precisely the category in the statement, independent of choices of $q$. Write $t^X_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$ and $t^Q_n:Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. The strict tower equation $q_n t^X_n=t^Q_n q_{n+1}$ becomes $G(q_n)G(t^X_n)=G(t^Q_n)G(q_{n+1})$. This proves compatibility before localization with every transition; no coherent choices of the separate homotopy inverses from step 2 are necessary. In particular, when $X_n=J$ and $t^X_n=s$, its image $TX$ has terms $GJ$ and transitions $G(s)$ by definition. Step 5 identifies this actual tower with its derived image.
